declared_proposition: Let D be dense in a complex Hilbert space H and q a Hermitian quadratic form on D. The form extends uniquely to a bounded Hermitian form on H if and only if |q(x)|<=C||x||^2 on D for some finite C. Positivity then passes to H. Pointwise Cauchy convergence on a countable dense core is not sufficient: the positive finite sections q_N(x)=sum_{k<=N} k|x_k|^2 stabilize on c_00 but their limit has q(e_k)=k and no bounded extension to l^2.
mathematical_argument: Necessity follows by restricting a bounded extension to D. For sufficiency, complex polarization and rescaling give |B(x,y)|<=2C||x||||y||, so B extends uniquely by density. The quadratic form of the extension is continuous, and nonnegativity passes from D to H. In the counterexample every finite-support vector is eventually unchanged by the truncations, while the unit coordinate values k are unbounded; a bounded extension would bound all of them by one common constant.

reproducible_computation.no_go_scope: This is an abstract extension theorem and an exact no-go for pointwise-only promotion. It proves no convergence or uniform admissible-norm bound for the actual Weil quadratic form and does not prove the Riemann hypothesis.

discarded_route: promoting pointwise Cauchy convergence on a dense countable core without one uniform continuity bound
remaining_gap: No uniform admissible-norm bound is proved for the actual pole-neutral Weil quadratic values.
claim_boundary: No RH proof. The exact continuity criterion is proved abstractly; its actual Weil-form premise remains open.
